Advances both destination addresses by 80 screen cells, the two foreground offsets by 800 and the two secondary offsets by 440, then starts the next pair.
Jump vector for copying the initial panel screen cells.
Jump vector for refreshing the decimal tally digits on the panel.
Jump vector for refreshing the packed-decimal balance display.
Jump vector for the display refresh at $1237.
Jump vector for the colour-RAM clear at $1306.
Jump vector for drawing twelve glyphs of a banner message.
Jump vector for the panel colour-RAM initialization.
Copies panel screen cells from $3894–$395B to $06D0–$0797 and from $395C–$39AB to $0798–$07E7, in the VIC screen page at $0400.
Starts by writing colour eight to the corresponding panel colour RAM cells beginning at $06CF's colour-RAM counterpart.
Patched immediate holding the packed panel value. Four right shifts extract the high digit, and $F3 converts it to the panel font's digit range.
Immediate A byte at $121B after the routine stores a panel digit. The following shifts and additions turn the nibbles into panel character codes beginning at $F3.
Looks up the screen character index from each staged row at $C000 and following 40-byte strides, then writes the corresponding stage colour from $9200 to colour RAM at $D800 and following rows.
High byte of the screen load for row 1. This step translates the tile at $C000,Y through $9200 and stores the colour at $D800,Y.
High byte of the screen load for row 2. This step translates the tile at $C028,Y through $9200 and stores the colour at $D828,Y.
High byte of the screen load for row 3. This step translates the tile at $C050,Y through $9200 and stores the colour at $D850,Y.
High byte of the screen load for row 4. This step translates the tile at $C078,Y through $9200 and stores the colour at $D878,Y.
High byte of the screen load for row 5. This step translates the tile at $C0A0,Y through $9200 and stores the colour at $D8A0,Y.
High byte of the screen load for row 6. This step translates the tile at $C0C8,Y through $9200 and stores the colour at $D8C8,Y.
High byte of the screen-cell load preceding $12A6. Use the resulting tile number to select from $9200 and update the corresponding colour-RAM cell.
High byte of the screen load for row 8. This step translates the tile at $C118,Y through $9200 and stores the colour at $D918,Y.
High byte of the screen load for row 9. This step translates the tile at $C140,Y through $9200 and stores the colour at $D940,Y.
High byte of the screen load for row 10. This step translates the tile at $C168,Y through $9200 and stores the colour at $D968,Y.
High byte of the screen load for row 11. This step translates the tile at $C190,Y through $9200 and stores the colour at $D990,Y.
High byte of the screen load for row 12. This step translates the tile at $C1B8,Y through $9200 and stores the colour at $D9B8,Y.
High byte of the screen load for row 13. This step translates the tile at $C1E0,Y through $9200 and stores the colour at $D9E0,Y.
High byte of the screen load for row 14. This step translates the tile at $C208,Y through $9200 and stores the colour at $DA08,Y.
High byte of the screen load for row 15. This step translates the tile at $C230,Y through $9200 and stores the colour at $DA30,Y.
Operand of the screen-cell fetch just before the stage tile-table lookup. Translate the fetched tile through $9200 and write the result to the indexed colour-RAM destination.
Low operand at $1316 for STA $DACF,Y. References from $1308 (STA), $131C (LDA), $1322 (STA).
High byte of the patched colour-RAM destination. The clear loop advances the destination by $F0 between passes, carrying into this byte.

Patches the message pointer from X/Y, selects $C700 or $0440 according to carry and clears 128 bytes. It masks each of twelve characters to six bits and copies eight glyph rows from $3000 at three-byte strides.
Low operand at $1367 for LDA BANNER_MESSAGE_BYTES,X. References from $132E (STX).
Operand of the source glyph load. Mask each code to six bits and multiply by eight to select its glyph at $3000.
Low operand at $1383 for LDA MESSAGE_FONT,X. References from $1374 (STA).
High byte of the patched banner font load at $1383. Store the selected glyph's eight rows three cells apart through $37.
Offsets used at $1354 to position the twelve message glyphs inside their sprite buffer.
Stored instruction sequence shifting alternating screen and colour rows in opposite directions. The branch at $13F5 targets $137B, which lies inside the message renderer in this snapshot.
Entry vector for the routine at $2A1D that advances the scroll counter and refreshes the displayed progress.
Entry vector that loads the stage quota from $73F9 into the scroll counter.
Jump entry that sets the temporary player flag in bit zero of $3F and loads $FF into $3D.
Jump entry that sets bit one of the player's flags at $3F.
Jumps to $2A49. The adjacent entry at $1412 sets lives to three, then clears both packed score fields and the listed zero-page game state.
Zero-page operand at the start of the stage-state reset. The following stores initialize shop and other mode flags using the same value in X.
Set the transition flags and initial scroll and colour values. Fill all five collected-heart slots with $FF before starting the stage.

Starts playfield setup by installing the line-zero IRQ at $16AD. Calls the level and player setup entry points, enables IRQs and waits for the game display to come back before falling into the restart path.
Runs the stage entry setup at $2A8A, sets $30 to one and calls the jump-table entry at $4000 before initialising the per-stage zero-page fields.
Immediate stage-start initialization flag. The first pass chooses entry fifteen and increments the flag. Later passes choose the nearest saved restart position.
Scans the first fifteen X entries at $A230, retaining the smallest distance from the reference column and patching the index read at $152E.
Operand in the stage-start comparison loop. Subtract the current table entry at $A230,X and complement the negative result before comparing it with the saved limit.
Immediate value in the descending setup scan. Carry clear replaces the byte with the current candidate and saves the candidate's index at $152F.
Immediate operand at $152E for LDX #$00. References from $1528 (STX).
Reads Y and X tile coordinates from the tables at $A240 and $A230, patches coordinate operands, and scales the X coordinate by eight before adding the screen origin offset.
Immediate starting coordinate quantum $63. Doubling it gives $C6. Subtracting $10 gives the paired position that is staged through X and Y.
Immediate frame selection at $1581. The intro installs player and auxiliary sprite frames, queues the GET READY banner, initializes the display and starts the countdown at $3A.
Take the low byte of the scroll position and rotate in the carry from the high byte. Save the half-column and combine it with the scaled coordinate derived from $16.
Immediate addend at $15FA. The remainder adjusts the saved continuation address, with separate paths for time expiry, game over and returning to the title setup.
Immediate mode gate. The enabled branch loads music and runs transition routines. The other branch tests the shop request and the special-room flag before ordinary gameplay initialization.
Immediate operand of $167B. With a pending redraw, clears this flag and derives the map pointer one column to either side of $0F/$10 according to bit seven of $08, then calls $1000.
Saves A, X and Y in $03-$05. Selects VIC bank $C000 via CIA2, loads the playfield's $D016 and $D018 values and resets sprite expansion, priority and X high bits for the top of the frame.

Operand of the first display-control load in the playfield IRQ. The setup selects VIC bank $C000, clears the sprite X-MSB, horizontal expansion and priority masks, and applies the saved scroll and memory selectors.
Immediate background-zero colour in the main playfield IRQ.
Immediate background-one colour loaded into X in the main playfield IRQ.
Immediate colour loaded into A for VIC background zero. X and Y supply the other two colours. The sprite mask comes from $36 when $742B is set.
Opcode of the transition-state load after the sprite-enable write. The setup at $8781 can patch this byte.
Patched opcode of the branch that bypasses the special display-state path.

Jump to $19A1 while the pause state is active. The fall-through path updates the entry sprite sequence, positioning its two sprites while $3A counts down and resetting their pointers and slots on expiry.
Immediate actor index used to walk the slot order at $0340. The slot picks the sprite colour and shape pointer written by this loop.
High byte in the store whose low operand is at $1779. The IRQ patches it from the active display page before assigning actor sprite positions and updating the player sprites.

Immediate addition operand at $17C8, also used at $172E to position the entry sprites. The following player path tests the frame's control state, then moves the player's X or advances the camera at its horizontal limit.
Retain the low three scroll bits in $06 and derive the selector at $0B. Update actor positions and take a new tile page from the pointer at $26.
Immediate Y byte at $18BE, read by $1903 and decremented there when nonzero. The firing path derives screen-relative tile coordinates and patches the lookup operands at $1924 and $1930.
Immediate zero written through $19 to erase a cell during the temporary scrolling effect. The cleanup sets $1B to $FF and clears $34 and $73A8.
Immediate signed direction for the temporary playfield cell effect. The negative path decrements the column and stops at underflow or the patched boundary.
Immediate special column limit. The forward search also stops at column 39. The row tables at $4FB9/$4FCB supply the starting screen address used to form the cell pointer.
Immediate low page selector ORed with $C0 at $194F to form the tile screen pointer. The code reads the tile, gets its properties and builds the eight-byte animated character at $FFE0.
Low operand at $1992 for LDA $FFFF,Y. References from $1971 (STA).
Patched source-page byte for the eight rows of the temporary scroll-effect character at $FFE0.
Address high byte of the write into the final character slot at $FFE0. The loop descends through its eight rows.
Services the sound path and uses the common IRQ tail to schedule $19AD on line $82.
Saves the interrupted registers in $5C–$5E, changes the raster comparator to $B2 and installs $1A59 in the IRQ vector. Acknowledges the current VIC IRQ before enabling interrupts.
Immediate enable for incrementing the colour transition phase. Phase two refreshes the stage colours, and phase four clears the enable.
Immediate enable for stepping the colour transition phase down. The phase-three path calls $118B. The enable clears when the signed phase goes below zero.
Immediate X flag at $1A0D. When set, the IRQ toggles the visible screen page, recalculates the draw page, then uses the scroll phase to build $D018.
Immediate toggle controlling alternate calls to the packed-decimal score and balance updates. The IRQ then restores A, X and Y from $5C through $5E.
Immediate background-zero colour for the panel half of the raster chain.
Immediate background-one colour loaded into X for the panel-side IRQ.
Immediate colour for VIC background zero in the panel-side IRQ. The same handler transfers the other two colours before checking $5A.
Copies the playfield's $D011 value into the operand at $1A95 and schedules the panel IRQ at raster $C2.
High address byte of the display-control latch store at $1A7D. It is patched by the setup at $878A.
Immediate raster-line byte loaded for the next IRQ.
Low byte of the IRQ continuation target loaded before $1A84 sets its high byte to $1A.
Saves the registers, waits in a short fixed loop, then sets CIA2 bank bits to three and switches the VIC memory pointers and colours for the status panel.
Immediate value for VIC control register one. This setup switches to bank zero, with screen $0400 and characters $0800, before writing the control and scroll registers.
Immediate panel background-zero colour installed at $1AB3.
Immediate panel background-one colour installed at $1AB6, updated by the palette animation.
Immediate byte loaded by LDY at $1AB1 and written to $D023. The IRQ also sets sprite modes, blinks a panel glyph and chooses a banner from the mode and message-index state.
Immediate gate at $1B14. The two paths select frame pointer $10 or $05 for sprite four, using the colour in $02CC and placing that sprite at X=$AC and Y=$CB.
Immediate enable for animating the first panel colour slot. Clear selects colour $0F and set calls the palette animation at $293D.
Immediate fallback sprite-seven colour $0F. After the store, load the phase for the panel colour update.
Immediate colour-effect countdown. Select the current colour from the table at $738E, save it to $1AB0, then decrement this counter.
Immediate byte loaded at $1B5F, copied into the panel colour setting at $1AB0. The tail selects the panel sprites and chooses player frames from the crouch, airborne and direction state.
Starting frame for the first room sprite. Add $11 when the direction at $1D is negative.
Immediate saved frame compared on entry. When the requested frame changes, update the horizontal offset and copy its sprite frame into the slot selected by X=0.
Starting frame for the companion room sprite. Apply the same negative-direction offset before comparing with the saved frame.
Immediate comparison operand at $1C4B. A different requested frame updates this byte and copies a new sprite into offset $40 through $275D.
Immediate load operand set while the panel toggles $32. The epilogue advances the four-way phase in $1E, clears the IRQ wait byte and schedules the gameplay, room or shop IRQ.
Installs the shop raster handler at $21A3 for line zero, using the IRQ tail $791A.
Saves the returning position in the operands at $1D68 and $1D6A, exchanges the room's character cells and positions the player using the first stage door coordinate pair.
Sets up pointers to packed stage data at $9098, screen RAM at $C000 and colour RAM at $D800. Draws two cells per source byte and stops at $9200.
Reads the low nibble for the first cell, then the high nibble for the second. Each selects a colour from $C6E0 and a character code from $4FDD.
Sets the room flag at $749C and calls the display synchronisation helper before returning to the IRQ state selection.
Immediate transition flag. The enabled path calls $2958, clears the flag and $749C, and sets $30 to one.
Saved immediate position restored to $16 when entering the room.
Patched X value restored into the player-position byte at $02 on entering the room. Store $FF in the room state, exchange character strips and branch into renderer setup.
Saves A, X and Y. The first pass configures VIC screen, colour and sprite registers, then the four scheduled passes display and test the room's object rows.
Immediate special-room entry gate. Zero goes to room video setup, and a nonzero value enters the later room update path.
Selects bank $C000 and screen $C000 with character data at $C000. Sets the multicolour registers and enables the room sprites when $742B permits.
Doubles six stored X coordinates and rotates each carry into the VIC high-X register. Also positions two sprites from the player's horizontal coordinate.
Gates movement on the room pass and player flags. Updates position through the joystick routine and patches the first collision-test operand.
Counts down the room update delay, then services audio and time. Selects an object slot when the pending flag at $1E67 is set.
Immediate index for the room sprite pointer table. Patch the pointer, update the raster selectors and apply any pending balance increment.
Immediate one-shot flag for selecting a special-room object slot. The enabled path clears the flag before calling $29A2.
Sets the row position for six sprites, picks a pointer from the object state and tests overlapping objects for collection. The IRQ hands off to the next row or to the status panel.
The immediate $20 at $1ECE. The sentinel path at $1ED3 substitutes $0E; both paths write to the current pointer at $C3FA,X.
Stops the play music, colours the shop rows, restores the saved music state and starts track selector six. The display is refreshed using the stored scroll progress.
Uses three 240-byte screen strips as indices into the tile colour lookup at $39AC and writes the resulting rows to colour RAM.
Uses the stage index at $998C to select the required scroll count from $73F9 and assigns it to the progress byte at $2709.

Decodes the heart colour from bits 3-5, searches the five stored colours at $02CD, and adds it when new. The fifth distinct colour displays the bonus message, clears the collection and invokes the life increment at $272C.
Immediate X loaded at $1FBD. The completion loop writes $FF back to the five collected-colour slots, then awards a life through $272C.
Compares the completed scroll count in the operand at $2709 with the stage requirement indexed from $73F9. The shop path branches to $20FE when equal.
Eight expected CIA keyboard return bytes for the stage-skip key-matrix scan at $200C.
A clear stage-skip flag enters the shop's ordinary selection path. Otherwise initialize the keyboard matrix scan.
Operand of the setup preceding the keyboard scan. The loop rotates the row selector, compares the port B result with $1FF0,X, and takes the stage select path only if every comparison matches.
Reads port 2 from $DC00. The low two direction bits move selection within six slots, including wrap from the end to the opposite end.
Uses the horizontal direction bits to change selection by three positions when the resulting index is in range. When both are released, tests fire separately.
Reads the selected item's two packed price bytes from $73C5 and $73BF and copies them to $73BD/$73BE for the price renderer.
Tests whether selection one is active. That path leaves the shop via $20BE. Other selections set the purchase latch at $2253.
Patched value restored into the saved scroll state at $11 after the room transition.
Operand of the load used to restore $12 before a playfield colour refresh. Clear $30 and advance $3A when it is already set before re-entering the main path at $167B.

Stores summary values for the completed-stage display, passes the banner pointer $72AF to the message routine at $269C, and waits for the raster chain's transition flags before loading the next payload.
Invokes the disk payload loader at $76D4. Tests the incremented load count at $02A7. At eight it calls the ending at $9080 and reloads payload one before restarting.
Runs the $4009 stage setup entry, waits for the IRQ-side transition latch to clear, calls $29F5, then returns to the stage entry loop.
Sets the shared transition byte $22B1 to one and polls until the IRQ side clears it.
Saves A, Y and X, then selects the shop character and screen bases with $D018=$BC and fine-scroll mode with $D016=$17.
Writes the selected vertical display control and three background colours, then sets sprite enable and multicolour state.
For each of the five collected-heart slots, selects the corresponding colour when the slot is occupied and stores the filled or empty sprite pointer.
Uses the four eight-entry arrays at $743D, $7445, $744D and $7455 to install sprite coordinates, pointers and colours.
Immediate count tested at $2252 and decremented before looking up and subtracting the selected item's packed-decimal price from the score.
Patched item index for shop purchasing. Item one takes its own branch. Other items fetch a price pointer from $73CB/$73D1.

Subtracts the price from the three-byte packed BCD money at $02AB-$02AD. A borrow skips the purchase. On success, checks item restrictions, writes back the balance, refreshes the HUD, and dispatches the selected item's effect through a patched JSR.
Preserves the remainder's high byte and checks the ownership bits in $3F before transferring the remaining score and calling the selected purchase handler.
Immediate high byte of the updated balance installed at $02AB before the lower bytes.
Patched immediate for the middle byte of the updated balance. Write the middle and low bytes before refreshing the panel and calling the selected purchase handler.
Low operand at $22AD for JSR $FFFF. References from $2262 (STA).
Patched high byte of the selected shop purchase-handler call at $22AD.
Immediate count tested by $22B0. A nonzero count is decremented before invoking the effect at $4003.
Calls the music tick when bit seven of $6B is clear and the gate at $2A56 is zero.
Immediate operand of $22C6. When the request is nonzero, this IRQ calls the 128-byte transfer at $7749 and decrements the request on carry. The main thread increments it at $214D and waits for zero.
Installs $22DB at raster line $68 through the shared IRQ exit at $791A.
Saves the interrupted registers, enables multicolour for sprite one, clears X expansion and prepares to replace seven sprite slots.
Writes seven sprite coordinates, pointers and colours for the upper shop row. The pointer stores use the $2C00 screen page, then the IRQ tail schedules line $96.
Saves the interrupted registers in $5C–$5E, installs the shop's next IRQ on raster line $97 and enables interrupts before processing the stage bonus display.
Immediate banner or bonus update state. The clear path skips the update and rejoins at $2397.
Immediate bonus-transfer selector. A nonzero value takes the path that adds the shop bonus to the score.
Counts down the bonus display timer and selects the next bonus field from the four entries at $7421.
Immediate table index for the branch that picks a replacement banner. $7421 supplies the display state and $7411/$7415 supply the message address sent to $269C.
Subtracts one from the displayed bonus counter in decimal mode and adds that field's configured amount to the player's score.
Immediate countdown. While nonzero, decrement it and start the descending 30-entry update using the screen addresses at $4F60/$4F7E.
Low operand at $23B3 for LDA $FFFF,X. References from $269C (STX).
Operand of the indexed character load. The following shifts and carry build a pointer into the eight-byte glyphs at $3000.
Low operand at $23CF for LDA $FFFF,X. References from $23C0 (STA).
Patched high byte of the indexed font read at $23CF. Store the eight glyph bytes three cells apart, then advance to the next banner cell or return from the IRQ.
Handles the shop row after the line-$96 bonus IRQ. The sprite loop starts at $2403.
Initialises X and Y to update four sprites. The data tables at $7479, $747D, $7481 and $7485 give coordinates, pointers and colours.
Doubles the sprite X coordinate and shifts the carry into the VIC high-X register. Writes the row's Y coordinate, pointer and colour.
Read the stage cell property with Y=2 and X=3, then save its high bit at $1F before entering the input handler.
Immediate mode gate for directional input. The selected path can bypass the joystick read or mask the two horizontal directions before processing it.
Reads the active-low port-2 joystick from CIA1 port A. The next instruction stores the sample in $1C. With left and fire held the monitored read changed from $7F to $6B.

Gates the duck on active-low down plus fire and rejects the case with up, left and right all pressed. It checks movement and terrain state before setting $5B. With down and fire held on a stage-one snapshot the store at $2479 set $5B to one.
Operand of the comparison preceding the match branch. A match uses a per-slot one-shot flag at $738C and the stage-supplied action index at $9090 to patch the call target at $24B3/$24B4.
Low operand at $24B2 for JSR $FFFF. References from $24A9 (STA).
Patched high byte of the stage action call at $24B2. After it returns, set the effect request to two and reload the panel icon state and colour.
Tests the right bit then the left bit of the joystick sample. Right sets $14 and $1D to one, and left sets them to $FF.
Immediate fire gate. While set, defer the fire action and clear the gate only after seeing the released input bit.
With fire pressed and the stage path active, queues effect three at $5100 and sets the projectile flag at $18BF. Initialises the two counters at $73A7 and $73A8 before entering the movement tail.
Immediate displacement-table index. Add the signed entry at $4F9C to player Y, then decrement the index and reset the movement phase on underflow.
Immediate phase at $2561, incremented until the comparison with $14 succeeds. The adjacent dispatch selects a movement path from $23, $5B or $22.
Immediate selector alternating between zero and one. Its value selects parallel flag and pending-state entries at $7396 and $7398.

Takes the low five joystick bits and tests for active-low up by itself. Compares position against different door-coordinate pairs in play and in the room state. The matching branches set the transition flags.
Immediate Y at $2635. The branch on bit seven of $22 selects one of the delta tables at $4F9C and $739B before adding the selected value to $02. The countdown updates this byte at $2651.
Immediate step counter for downward movement. It increments while preparing the displacement, resets to eight below Y=$E0, and sets the panel transition flag in $2D.
Patch the source pointer for the banner draw at $23B3 from X and Y, then request a draw through $2398.
Clear two consecutive 160-cell strips at $04C0–$05FF. Read offset $69 of the setup record through $7C and XOR it with $C4 to obtain the mode byte at $7A.
Splits the two price bytes at $73BD/$73BE into four nibbles. The digit helper multiplies each nibble by four and rewrites the shop screen template.
Multiply the glyph index by four and add $41 to get its first character code. Write four consecutive codes into a two-by-two group across the two shop screen rows.
Clears six progress screen cells and, when progress is nonzero, selects the stage's letter stream from $73EB/$73F2. Copies the collected number of letters after masking each to six bits.
Immediate gate for the stage-indexed scan. When enabled, patch the source operand at $271E/$271F from the low and high tables at $73EB/$73F2.
Low operand at $271D for LDA $FFFF,X. References from $2712 (STA).
High byte of the selected progress source address. Mask the fetched character to six bits before copying it to the shop display field and repeat for the enabled number of cells.
Increments the life count at $02AF unless it is already nine, then refreshes its displayed digit.
Convert the life count at $02AF to its panel glyph by adding $F3 and write the resulting character to $077C.
Draws the packed decimal minutes in A and seconds at $24 in the HUD, adding $F3 to each decimal digit to get its glyph code.
Convert both nibbles of the packed value in A into panel digit codes by adding $F3. Store the high and low digits in adjacent cells.
Frame number A chooses a 64-byte slot in the sheet beginning at $8800. X patches the destination low byte in bank $C000. The inner loop copies 63 visible sprite bytes.
Copies sprite rows from the patched source at $2775 to the patched destination at $2778, counting Y down from $3E.
Low operand at $2775 for LDA RESIDENT_SPRITE_FRAME_08,Y. References from $2767 (STA).
Patched high byte of the source sprite frame address at $2775.
Patched low destination byte of the sprite bitmap store. The loop proceeds downwards until all 63 visible bytes have been written.
Clear both arrays of six actor X coordinate bytes at $0360 and $0366.
Places the first two sprites at Y=$70. Sets their single-colour display, moves them using the VIC low and high X registers, and installs frame pointers $1C and $1D in both screen pages.

Add the two-byte packed-decimal increment at $50/$51 to the three-byte wallet at $02AB–$02AD, clear the increment and refresh the wallet display. Live stepping at $27F5 confirmed a carry from 009999 to 010000 while the score stayed at 001234.
Add the pending packed-decimal increment at $46/$47 to the score at $02A8–$02AA. Live stepping from 009999 with an increment of one reached 010000.
Immediate life-award gate. On an enabled match with the table at $7363, call the capped life increment and decrement the gate before clearing the tally increment bytes.

Decrements the tick divider at $2A. When it passes through zero and $13 allows a tick, resets it to $30 and subtracts one in BCD from seconds at $24. A borrow wraps seconds to $59 and decrements minutes at $25. At zero it sets the out-of-time flags at $33 and $13.
Acts when phase $1E is zero. While bit 0 of $3F is set, counts down $3D, alternates a colour setting late in the countdown, and clears the bit at expiry.
Patched zero test for the player-colour choice. The zero path selects colour $0A. The other path reaches the alternative colour store by entering the operand of BIT.
Shift the two-byte scroll position at $0F/$10 right once, then combine it with the scaled player coordinate derived from $16 minus $59.
Saved half-scroll column added to the scaled player column. Return the combined column in Y.
Convert the position at $16 into an eight-pixel row index after subtracting $11. Return that row in Y and the value at $739A plus three in A.
Multiply the supplied row by eight and add $11 to form the pixel coordinate at $16, then move the column from Y into A.
Multiply the value in A by eight and add $0C to form the pixel coordinate at $02.
Converts the input horizontal position and $02 vertical position into a cell address through the row-base tables at $4FB9 and $4FCB. The sign flag from $749B controls the high-byte adjustment.
Adds the selected row displacement to the current map pointer, patches the indexed load, and checks its row bound. In the stage path with $749B negative it translates the tile through $9200.
Low operand at $2927 for LDX F_C219,Y. References from $2915 (STA).
High byte of the indexed screen-cell fetch at $2927. Negative values at $749B select the stage property table at $9200. Nonnegative values return zero for tile $5A and $80 for other tiles.
Decrement the selected slot's colour delay. On underflow, reset the delay to four and decrement the palette index, wrapping that index to six before looking up the colour.
Set A to $5B and Y to zero before entering the common display transition at $2962.
Display restore entry. Set the IRQ control operand to $1B and use the flag at $59 to wait for two raster handshakes.
Tests the self-modified player X and Y coordinates against the room object column and row tables. Carry set rejects the overlap.
Immediate coordinate reduced by the indexed offset at $7489 and then by three. Negative results take the compensation path.
Immediate compensation added in the negative coordinate path. The sign test after the addition decides whether the compensated position is accepted.
Immediate coordinate reduced by the indexed offset at $748F and then by nine. Negative results take the companion compensation path.
Immediate addition in the compensated coordinate path. Compare the result against $80 to return the boundary decision in carry.
Selects either of the two 24-entry object groups at $4F00. Tries four bounded random indices before falling back to the scan at $29CA.
Immediate starting index for the fallback scan of the selected group in $4F00. Scan up to 24 entries and replace the first nonzero entry found with $80.
Remaining random attempts to find a room object slot before using the fallback scan.
